nodes.title: Async I/O Engine and Group Commit
nodes.description: Covers the pluggable I/O backend system (Mmap, Pread, IoUring), ExtentList coalescing, io_uring capability gating, async read engine with inline fast-path, and async write engine with group commit for DurabilityMode::Strict.
nodes.body:
# Async I/O Engine and Group Commit OIFS separates metadata operations from payload data reading. Filesystem metadata (superblocks, bitmaps, inodes, indirect pointer blocks, and directory indices) resides on the shared `MAP_SHARED` memory map for zero-copy, low-overhead access. File payloads can be large, cold, and scattered across physical blocks—reading them through the mmap means every uncached page is a synchronous page fault, one fault at a time. P3.2 introduced a pluggable data-block read engine (`src/io_engine.rs`) that decouples physical payload I/O from memory-mapped page faults, enabling applications to select between three backends: **Mmap**, **Pread**, and **IoUring**. In v1.4.0 the async write pipeline adds a dedicated group-commit thread that merges concurrent `DurabilityMode::Strict` operations behind a single `flush()` barrier. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph ReadPath ["DiskManager::read_at / read_at_batch"] Guard["Acquire Read Lock (inner.read())"] Prepare["read_at_prepare: Block Traversal + Extent Coalescing"] Extents["ExtentList (Contiguous Disk + Buffer Range Merge)"] Select{"IoBackend Selection"} end subgraph MmapPath ["Mmap (Default)"] MmapRead["read_mmap: memcpy from mmap slice"] end subgraph PreadPath ["Pread"] PreadLoop["read_pread: file.read_exact_at per extent"] end subgraph UringPath ["IoUring (Linux 5.15+ / RHEL 9.3+)"] Checkout["RingPool::checkout (64-entry ring)"] Populate["Populate SQEs (split >1MiB extents)"] Submit["submit_and_wait(1)"] Reap["Reap CQEs, handle short reads / transient errors"] Checkin["RingPool::checkin (cache up to 16)"] end Guard --> Prepare --> Extents --> Select Select -->|Mmap| MmapRead Select -->|Pread| PreadLoop Select -->|IoUring| Checkout --> Populate --> Submit --> Reap --> Checkin style MmapPath fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32 style PreadPath fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#ef6c00 style UringPath fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1565c0 ``` --- ## 1. IoBackend Architecture and Selection The `IoBackend` enum defines three distinct data-block retrieval strategies ([src/io_engine.rs#L36-L51](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L36-L51)): | Backend | Value | Mechanism | Platforms | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `IoBackend::Mmap` (Default) | 0 | `memcpy` directly from the shared memory mapping | All | | `IoBackend::Pread` | 1 | Positional `pread(2)` syscall per coalesced extent | All Unix | | `IoBackend::IoUring` | 2 | Batched async submission to a pooled `io_uring` ring | Linux ≥ 5.6, `io_uring` cargo feature | All backends read through the standard OS page cache without `O_DIRECT`, ensuring that recently written dirty pages (including uncommitted mutations under `DurabilityMode::Lazy`) are immediately visible across all backends ([src/io_engine.rs#L1-L25](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L1-L25)). Backend selection is configurable via: - **Environment variable**: `OIFS_IO_BACKEND=mmap|pread|io_uring` (case-insensitive; aliases: `uring`, `iouring`, `io-uring`). Read once at `DiskManager` construction via `IoBackend::from_env()` ([src/io_engine.rs#L34-L35](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L34-L35)). - **Programmatic Rust API**: `DiskManager::set_io_backend(backend)` or builder-style `DiskManager::with_io_backend(backend)` ([src/disk.rs#L1974-L1985](repo://src/disk.rs#L1974-L1985)). - **FFI**: `oifs_set_io_backend(handle, backend_u8)` and `oifs_get_io_backend(handle)` ([src/ffi.rs#L740-L775](repo://src/ffi.rs#L740-L775)). ```rust // Querying and configuring the backend let dm = DiskManager::open("data.oifs", 10 * 1024 * 1024)?; let effective = dm.set_io_backend(IoBackend::IoUring); assert_eq!(dm.io_backend(), effective); // effective backend after gating assert_eq!(dm.requested_io_backend(), IoBackend::IoUring); // what was asked for ``` Requesting `IoUring` where it is unavailable never fails; `IoBackend::resolve()` transparently falls back to `Pread`, and the effective backend is reported separately from the requested one ([src/io_engine.rs#L60-L68](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L60-L68)). --- ## 2. ExtentList Block Coalescing Non-contiguous files incur high syscall or SQE overhead if dispatched one 4 KiB block at a time. OIFS solves this through `ExtentList`, which merges contiguous physical disk runs **and** destination buffer offsets on `push` ([src/io_engine.rs#L232-L287](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L232-L287)): ```rust pub fn push(&mut self, disk_offset: u64, buf_offset: usize, len: usize) { if len == 0 { return; } if let Some(last) = self.extents.last_mut() && last.disk_offset.checked_add(last.len as u64) == Some(disk_offset) && last.buf_offset.checked_add(last.len) == Some(buf_offset) && let Some(new_len) = last.len.checked_add(len) { last.len = new_len; return; } self.extents.push(ReadExtent { disk_offset, buf_offset, len }); } ``` A file whose blocks were allocated contiguously therefore collapses into a single extent, i.e. a single `pread` / single SQE regardless of its size in blocks. This applies uniformly to all three backends. --- ## 3. IoUring Capability Gating The `IoUring` backend is only enabled when all conditions hold ([src/io_engine.rs#L115-L210](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L115-L210)): - Running on Linux (`target_os = "linux"`). - Crate compiled with the `io_uring` cargo feature. - Kernel version ≥ 5.15 **or** RHEL 9.3+ backport (kernel `5.14.0-362+` with `el9` in release string). - `io_uring` syscall permitted (not blocked by `kernel.io_uring_disabled` sysctl or seccomp). The probe runs once per process via `OnceLock`. If any check fails, `IoEngine::new()` quietly falls back to `Pread`. The fallback is reported through `DiskManager::io_backend()` (effective) vs `DiskManager::requested_io_backend()` (requested). An environment variable `OIFS_ALLOW_PRE_5_15=1` can override the kernel version check for testing. --- ## 4. RingPool and Safe Completion Loop Each `IoEngine` with `effective() == IoUring` owns a `RingPool` ([src/io_engine.rs#L512-L589](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L512-L589)): - **Pool size**: Up to 16 idle rings cached; additional rings created under contention are dropped after use. - **Ring parameters**: 64 submission queue entries, 1 MiB max per `IORING_OP_READ` SQE (larger extents are split). - **Checkout/Checkin**: `RingPool::checkout()` reuses an idle ring or creates a fresh one; `RingPool::checkin()` returns it to the pool. The per-request read loop ([src/io_engine.rs#L620-L707](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L620-L707)) guarantees **memory safety** by never returning while any SQE is in flight: ```text 1. Populate SQEs from pending ops until ring depth (64) or ops exhausted. 2. ring.submit_and_wait(1) – blocks until ≥1 CQE available. 3. Reap completions: on short read, advance pointer and resubmit remainder; on transient error (EINTR/EAGAIN/EBUSY), requeue; on hard error, abort process (kernel may still be writing into caller buffers). 4. Repeat until inflight == 0. 5. Checkin ring, return result. ``` This invariant prevents use-after-free of the caller's buffers. --- ## 5. Read Path: read_at / read_at_batch `DiskManager::read_at_batch` processes multiple `ReadRequest` items under a single read lock, planning extents for each, then submitting the batch to the I/O engine ([src/disk.rs#L4737-L4790](repo://src/disk.rs#L4737-L4790)): ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant DM as DiskManager participant Guard as inner.read() participant Prep as read_at_prepare participant Engine as IoEngine participant Backend as Mmap/Pread/IoUring Caller->>DM: read_at_batch(requests) DM->>Guard: Acquire read lock loop For each request Guard->>Prep: read_at_prepare(inode, offset, buf) Prep-->>Guard: ExtentList (or inline copy) end DM->>Engine: read_backing(file, backing, targets) Engine->>Backend: Execute coalesced extents Backend-->>Engine: Data in caller buffers Engine-->>DM: Ok / IoError DM-->>Caller: Vec> ``` `read_at_prepare` traverses the inode's block pointers (direct, single/double/triple indirect) and either: - Copies directly from mmap when `extents = None` and `StorageMode::Mmap`. - Appends to `ExtentList` (coalescing contiguous runs) when `extents = Some`. - Zero-fills holes (unallocated blocks). --- ## 6. Async Read Engine: Inline Fast-Path `DiskManager::read_at_async` and `read_data_async` return an `OifsAsyncTask` ([src/disk.rs#L9015-L9170](repo://src/disk.rs#L9015-L9170)). The task first probes the **Inline Fast-Path** on the calling thread: 1. Acquire `inner.try_read()` (non-blocking). 2. Look up inode (cache or mmap decode). 3. If `Seekable64K` chunked: check `ChunkReadCache`. 4. If compressed/encrypted: check `DecodedBlobCache`. 5. If raw file: try `DataPageCache` (FileIo mode) or mmap. If **all** needed bytes are resident, `OifsAsyncTask::ready(Ok(buf))` is returned instantly (~50 ns, zero heap allocation, no thread hop). Only on cache miss, lock contention, or cold decode is `OifsAsyncTask::spawn()` used to dispatch to the background async pool (2–8 worker threads, `oifs-async-N` naming). ```mermaid flowchart TD A["read_at_async()"] --> B{"try_read() lock
+ inode resolve
+ cache probes"} B -->|All caches hit| C["OifsAsyncTask::ready
Inline Fast-Path"] B -->|Any miss| D["OifsAsyncTask::spawn
Background pool"] C --> E["Caller .await = Poll::Ready"] D --> F["Worker thread runs
read_at_vec()"] F --> G["Complete via AsyncTaskState"] ``` The `OifsAsyncTask` implements `Future`, `is_ready()`, `try_take()`, `wait()`, and `wait_for_completion()` for maximum integration flexibility. --- ## 7. Async Write Engine: Group Commit `DiskManager` exposes async write operations that route through a **dedicated group-commit worker thread** ([src/disk.rs#L8538-L8905](repo://src/disk.rs#L8538-L8905)): - `create_file_with_data_async` - `write_data_async` - `flush_async_task` ### Group-Commit Protocol 1. Each async write submits a `GroupWriteOp` containing `(DiskManager, run_fn, complete_fn)` to a lock-free MPSC queue (`oifs-group-commit` thread). 2. Worker wakes, drains up to 128 ops into a local `batch` vec. 3. Enters `DeferStrictSyncGuard::enter()` (thread-local flag). 4. Executes each `run_fn(&dm)` **without** individual `flush()` calls. 5. After batch execution (and harvesting newly arrived ops up to 128 total), exits the guard. 6. **Deduplicates** `DiskManager` inner `Arc` pointers among successful `Strict` ops; issues **one `flush()` per distinct DiskManager**. 7. Propagates any flush error to all ops sharing that DiskManager. 8. Invokes each `complete_fn(Result)`. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C1 as Caller 1 (Strict) participant C2 as Caller 2 (Strict) participant GW as Group-Commit Worker participant DM1 as DiskManager A participant DM2 as DiskManager B C1->>GW: submit_group_write_op(dmA, write1, cb1) C2->>GW: submit_group_write_op(dmA, write2, cb2) GW->>GW: batch [op1, op2] GW->>DM1: DeferStrictSyncGuard::enter() GW->>DM1: run write1() GW->>DM1: run write2() GW->>DM1: DeferStrictSyncGuard::drop() GW->>DM1: flush() (single barrier) GW-->>C1: cb1(Ok) GW-->>C2: cb2(Ok) ``` **Result**: Concurrent `Strict` writers to the same image share one physical `msync`/`fdatasync`, preserving strict durability with minimal I/O amplification. --- ## 8. FFI Async API Surface The C FFI exposes both **polling** and **callback-based** async interfaces ([src/ffi.rs#L1583-L1880](repo://src/ffi.rs#L1583-L1880)): | Function | Mode | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `oifs_read_at_async_cb` | Callback | Async positional read with completion callback | | `oifs_create_file_with_data_async_cb` | Callback | Async file creation + initial write (group-commit) | | `oifs_write_file_async_cb` | Callback | Async file write (group-commit) | | `oifs_async_poll` / `oifs_async_wait` | Polling | Manual future polling / blocking wait | | `oifs_async_free` | Cleanup | Blocks on `wait_on_drop` barrier for read tasks | The `OIFSAsyncFuture` wrapper around `OifsAsyncTask` sets `wait_on_drop = true` for read tasks, ensuring `oifs_async_free` does not return until the background read finishes writing into the caller's buffer—preventing use-after-free. --- ## 9. Configuration Summary | Setting | Mechanism | Scope | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Backend selection | `OIFS_IO_BACKEND` env var / `DiskManager::set_io_backend` | Process / Instance | | Kernel override | `OIFS_ALLOW_PRE_5_15=1` | Process (testing) | | Async pool size | `available_parallelism().clamp(2, 8)` | Process (auto) | | Group-commit batch cap | 128 ops | Per worker wake | | Ring pool idle cap | 16 rings | Per IoEngine | --- ## 10. Key Invariants - **Metadata never uses pluggable backends**: Superblock, bitmaps, inodes, indirect blocks, directories always use the shared mmap. - **All backends are cache-coherent**: No `O_DIRECT`; dirty pages from `Lazy` writes visible to `Pread`/`IoUring` immediately. - **Extent coalescing is lossless**: `ExtentList::push` preserves exact byte ranges; `total_bytes()` equals sum of inputs. - **IoUring never leaks in-flight SQEs**: The read loop aborts the process on hard `io_uring_enter` failure with pending SQEs. - **Inline Fast-Path is zero-allocation**: `OifsAsyncTask::ready` uses stack-only `inline_ready` field. - **Group commit deduplicates by DiskManager identity**: `Arc::as_ptr(&dm.inner)` used as key; one `flush()` per distinct image.

nodes.title: Block & Inode Allocation
nodes.description: Documents the bitmap-based block allocator (SimpleBlockAllocator), inode allocator, free space tracking, allocation strategies (hints, contiguous runs), multi-block bitmap layout (v3), hardware-accelerated tzcnt scanning, BitmapSliceMut write-through mirrors for FileIo mode, and allocation simulation for WAL transactions.
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership

Block and inode allocation is centralized in `SimpleBlockAllocator` (`src/allocator.rs`) operating on 4 KB bitmap slices. The `DiskManagerInner` (`src/disk.rs`) owns the actual bitmap slices in the mmapped image (or in-memory mirrors under `FileIo` mode) and drives allocation through cached search hints stored in `free_block_hint` and `free_inode_hint`. Every allocation, deallocation, directory write, and indirect-block expansion on the write path goes through this machinery, so it is the single authority over which physical blocks are free or in use.

For journaled images, allocation is first simulated against in-memory bitmap copies via `AllocSim` (`src/journal.rs`) before any on-disk metadata is mutated. `AllocSim` mirrors `SimpleBlockAllocator` semantics exactly (same hint handling, same "first free bit at or after hint" rule), so the IDs it predicts are the IDs the real allocator will hand out when the transaction is applied.

## On-disk bitmap representation (v3 multi-block layout)

A bitmap is a flat bit array stored in one or more 4 KB blocks. Bit `0` means free and bit `1` means allocated. `SuperBlock` (`src/superblock.rs`) records where each bitmap lives and how many blocks each spans:

- Inode bitmap starts at `inode_bitmap_block` (block 1 in legacy layout; spans `inode_bitmap_blocks()` blocks in v3), tracking inodes from ID 0.
- Data bitmap starts at `data_bitmap_block` (block 2 in legacy; spans `data_bitmap_blocks()` blocks in v3), tracking data blocks starting at `data_block_start`.

The v3 layout computes `inode_bitmap_blocks = inode_count.div_ceil(BITMAP_BLOCK_BITS).max(1)` and `data_bitmap_blocks` derived from the recorded `data_block_start` and `inode_table_block` offsets. Bit index mapping: for the data bitmap, the bit index for a given `block_id` is `block_id - data_block_start`. The inode bitmap uses a direct 0-based index (inode ID == bit index).

Two views wrap the raw bytes:

- `BitmapRef` (`src/bitmap.rs`) — read-only view used for analysis, scanning, and fsck.
- `Bitmap` (`src/bitmap.rs`) — mutable view that forwards `set`/`clear` and delegates search helpers to a `BitmapRef`.

Under `StorageMode::FileIo`, the on-disk bitmaps are mirrored in memory (`FileBacking.inode_bitmap` / `data_bitmap` in `src/storage.rs`). Mutable access is provided through `BitmapSliceMut` (see below).

## 64-bit word scanning and hardware `tzcnt`

The bitmap deliberately processes 64 bits (8 bytes) per CPU word instead of bit by bit. The key operations in `BitmapRef` all use `chunks_exact(8)`:

- `find_first_free_from` masks out bits before the search start with `(1u64 << bit_in_chunk) - 1`, then locates the first zero bit using `(!masked_word).trailing_zeros()` — a single hardware `tzcnt` instruction on x86/ARM.
- `for_each_set_bit` (used by fsck, defragmentation, and `analyze_fragmentation`) iterates set bits with `word &= word - 1` to clear the lowest set bit each cycle, yielding only as many iterations as there are allocated blocks.
- `analyze_fragmentation` (`src/disk/maintenance.rs`) additionally special-cases whole words equal to `0` (all free) or `u64::MAX` (all used) so densely packed regions are scanned in constant time.

These optimizations deliver 11×–13.4× faster free-block scans and ~7.4× fsck speedup over bit-by-bit scanning.

## Allocation hints for amortized O(1) sequential allocation

Before hints, allocating many blocks sequentially re-scanned the bitmap from bit 0 every time, producing O(N²) behavior. `allocate_with_hint` (`src/allocator.rs`) accepts an optional hint block ID and translates it to a bit index (`hint - start_block_offset`) before calling `find_next_free_wrapped`.

`DiskManagerInner` keeps two hints and advances them after each allocation:

- `allocate_block` reads `free_block_hint`, allocates, then sets `free_block_hint = blk + 1`.
- Inode allocation in `create_entry_internal` reads `free_inode_hint`, allocates, then sets `free_inode_hint = new_inode_id + 1`.

When a hint points past the end of the bitmap, `find_next_free_wrapped` wraps around and searches from bit 0 for a bit below the hint, so allocation is guaranteed to find space whenever one exists. Freeing a block updates the hint downward (`min_freed_blk < free_block_hint`), keeping sequential allocation compact.

## Contiguous-run allocation for seekable 64K chunks

Seekable 64 KiB chunked files (`INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K`) require each chunk to occupy a contiguous run of physical blocks so that a chunk can be read with a single I/O operation. `SimpleBlockAllocator::allocate_contiguous` (`src/allocator.rs`) finds the first run of `count` consecutive free bits starting from a hint, using `BitmapRef::find_contiguous_free_wrapped`. The allocator scans 64-bit words and skips entirely used words in O(1), then checks candidate runs bit-by-bit only when a mixed word is encountered.

The write path (`commit_prepared_chunked_write` in `src/disk/chunked.rs`) stages through `AllocSim`:

1. For each chunk, `sim.alloc_contiguous(backing, prepared.blocks_needed)` reserves a contiguous run in the simulator's data-bitmap copy.
2. The run is recorded in the WAL via `SetDataBitmapRange { start_block, count, allocated: true }` (coalesced from individual `SetDataBitmap` ops).
3. Payload bytes are written into the newly allocated blocks in the mmap.
4. Old chunk blocks (if any) are freed via `sim.free_contiguous` and `SetDataBitmapRange { allocated: false }`.
5. The inode's chunk-entry pointer is updated to point at the new run (`sim_set_logical_chunk_entry` emits a `WriteBlockSlice` for the pointer table entry).

This guarantees that every seekable chunk maps to a single contiguous physical extent, eliminating intra-chunk seeks.

## BitmapSliceMut: write-through mirrors for FileIo mode

Under `StorageMode::FileIo` there is no mmap; the filesystem image is accessed via `pread`/`pwrite`. To keep bitmap mutations coherent, `DiskManagerInner` provides mutable access through `BitmapSliceMut` (`src/storage.rs`):

```rust
pub(crate) struct BitmapSliceMut<'a> {
    slice: &'a mut [u8],
    file_writeback: Option<(&'a File, u64)>,  // (file handle, file offset of bitmap start)
    dirty_range: Option<(usize, usize)>,     // narrowed byte range [start..end)
}
```

- `inode_bitmap_slice_mut()` and `data_bitmap_slice_mut()` on `ImageBacking` return a `BitmapSliceMut` borrowing the in-memory mirror.
- `DerefMut` allows direct byte mutation (`slice[byte] |= mask`).
- `set_dirty_range(byte_start, byte_end)` and `set_dirty_bits(start_bit, bit_count)` narrow the flush range.
- On `Drop`, `flush_writeback()` is called automatically: under `FileIo` it issues a `pwrite` of the dirty range to the bitmap's file offset; under `Mmap` it is a no-op (the mmap is already coherent).
- Explicit `flush_writeback()` is also available for callers that need synchronous persistence before the guard drops.

## Allocation simulation (`AllocSim`) for WAL transactions

Journaled images must never mutate on-disk metadata before the transaction is logged. `AllocSim` (`src/journal.rs`) provides a copy-on-write simulator:

- It clones the inode and data bitmap slices on first use (`ensure_data_bitmap` is lazy for data-only transactions).
- It wraps `SimpleBlockAllocator` to perform `alloc_block`, `alloc_contiguous`, `free_contiguous` against the copies.
- It tracks `fresh_blocks` (blocks allocated during the transaction) and `pointers` (simulated indirect pointer updates).
- On commit, the simulator's `free_block_hint` and `free_inode_hint` are copied back to `DiskManagerInner`, so subsequent allocations resume from the predicted state.

This design ensures that the WAL can roll back a failed transaction by simply discarding the simulator; no on-disk state is touched until `apply_journal_ops` runs.

## Inode allocation and free inode tracking

Inode allocation uses the same `SimpleBlockAllocator` machinery with a zero `start_block_offset` (inode ID == bit index). The inode bitmap may track more IDs than the inode table can hold (`usable_inode_count`); `find_next_free_bounded` limits the search to valid table capacity. Allocation proceeds as:

1. Read `free_inode_hint`.
2. `BitmapRef::find_next_free_bounded(hint, usable_inode_count)` → `new_inode_id`.
3. If `new_inode_id >= usable_inode_count`, release the bit and return `NoSpace`.
4. Set bit, update `free_inode_hint = new_inode_id + 1`.
5. Under `FileIo`, `BitmapSliceMut::set_dirty_bits(id, 1)` narrows the pwrite to the affected byte.

Freeing an inode clears the bit and rewinds `free_inode_hint = min(free_inode_hint, inode_id)` so newly freed IDs are reused quickly.

## Free space tracking and fragmentation analysis

`analyze_fragmentation` (`src/disk/maintenance.rs`) walks the data bitmap once using the same 64-bit word fast path:

- Counts `used_blocks`, `free_blocks`, `free_runs`, `largest_free_run`, `total_gap_size`.
- Special-cases `word == 0` (64 free blocks in O(1)) and `word == u64::MAX` (64 used blocks in O(1)).
- Computes `avg_gap_size = total_gap_size / free_runs`.
- Computes `fragmentation_ratio = (free_runs - 1) / (free_blocks - 1)` (0.0 = perfectly contiguous free space, 1.0 = maximum fragmentation).

This analysis is used by the defragmenter and exposed via CLI/FUSE/NFS/IPC for monitoring.

## Block deallocation and hint rewind

`free` and `free_contiguous` clear the corresponding bits and update `free_block_hint` downward if the freed range starts before the current hint. This keeps the allocator's search window compact after truncation or file deletion, avoiding unnecessary scans past large freed regions.

## Indirect block allocation

Indirect blocks are allocated via the same `allocate_block` / `allocate_contiguous` path. `get_or_alloc_indirect_child` and `get_or_alloc_block_for_write` resolve or allocate pointer entries on demand, always verifying that both the parent indirect block and any child block live inside the data area (`is_data_block` check). This ensures the allocator never hands out metadata-region blocks for payload data.

nodes.title: Compression Pipeline and SIMD Filters
nodes.description: How OIFS combines zstd compression (stream append, seekable 64K chunked with COW extent swap, read-modify-recompress fallback) with Blosc2-style pre-compression SIMD filters (Delta, ByteShuffle, BitShuffle, TruncPrecision). Covers ZstdContextPool, persistent scoped worker pool, filter recommendation engine, DecodedBlobCache and ChunkReadCache.
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership The write, read, and filter pipeline live across several modules: - `write_data_with_filters` ([`src/disk.rs#L4432-L4728`]) orchestrates the full staging sequence — pre-compression filter → zstd compression → encryption. - `filters.rs` ([`src/filters.rs`]) provides the filter primitives, `FilterConfig` stored on the inode, the native C-Blosc2 wrapper, and entropy analysis. - `disk/chunked.rs` ([`src/disk/chunked.rs`]) implements the seekable 64KB chunked fast path (random reads/writes, COW extent swap). - `disk/caches.rs` ([`src/disk/caches.rs`]) provides `DecodedBlobCache` (whole-file decoded blob cache for non-seekable compressed/encrypted files) and `ChunkReadCache` (per-chunk decompression cache for seekable files). - `zstd_pool.rs` ([`src/zstd_pool.rs`]) manages thread-local Zstd contexts and a persistent scoped worker pool used for parallel chunk compression/decompression. ## The write-stage pipeline Every initial write (`file_offset == 0`) flows through `plan_write_prepared` ([`src/disk.rs#L881-L1057`]), which applies a fixed, ordered staging pipeline. The reverse order is used on read (decrypt → decompress → unapply filter). 1. **Pre-compression filter** — `apply_filters_cow` transforms the raw payload into a more compressible form. This runs *before* compression so filters can collapse Shannon entropy that a generic LZ77 compressor cannot reuse. 2. **Compression** — governed by `CompressionMode` ([`src/disk.rs#L66-L78`]): - `Always`: always zstd (level 0). - `Never`: never compress. - `Auto` (default): compress only when the filtered data is ≥ 8KB, and only keep the compressed result if it is actually smaller than the working data. - `Stream { level }`: full-file stream compression with explicit Zstd level. - `Seekable { chunk_size, level }`: fixed 64KB chunked compression with O(1) random access. 3. **Encryption** — if a key is present, the (already compressed) data is encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 and a fresh per-file nonce. Compressing before encrypting preserves compression ratio while keeping ciphertext entropy flat. The ordering filter→compress→encrypt is why both `inode.compressed_size` (physical) and `inode.size` (logical) are tracked separately, and why the filter flags (`filter_typesize`, `filter_delta`, `filter_shuffle`, `filter_bitshuffle`) must be recorded on the inode to reverse the pipeline on read. ## Zero-copy filter staging `apply_filters_cow` ([`src/filters.rs#L829-L835`]) returns a `Cow<[u8]>`: `Cow::Borrowed(data)` (zero allocation) when the filter is inactive or the typesize is not one of {1, 2, 4, 8}, and `Cow::Owned` only when a pipeline actually runs. On the common unfiltered/unencrypted path this eliminates every intermediate buffer copy — reported as up to ~28,500x speedup on 1MB payloads — and lets the uncompressed bytes flow straight into the write. ## Compression pipeline flow diagram ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph WritePath["Write Pipeline (file_offset == 0)"] A["Raw Payload"] --> B["apply_filters_cow
(FilterConfig → FilterPipeline)"] B --> C{"CompressionMode"} C -->|Always/Auto/Stream| D["zstd_pool::compress_frame
(thread-local CCtx)"] C -->|Seekable| E["write_chunked_64k_pipeline
(64KB chunks)"] C -->|Never| F["Pass through"] D --> G["Encryption (XChaCha20-Poly1305)
if key present"] E --> G F --> G G --> H["Write to disk"] end subgraph ReadPath["Read Pipeline"] I["Read from disk"] --> J{"Encrypted?"} J -->|Yes| K["Decrypt"] J -->|No| L K --> L{"Compressed?"} L -->|Stream| M["zstd_pool::decompress_frame_into
(thread-local DCtx)"] L -->|Seekable 64K| N["read_at_chunked_64k
(single chunk decode)"] L -->|None| O["Direct copy"] M --> P["unapply_filters_cow
(reverse pipeline)"] N --> P O --> P P --> Q["Caller buffer"] end subgraph FilterPipeline["FilterPipeline.apply / unapply"] direction LR FP1["Delta"] --> FP2["ByteShuffle"] FP2 --> FP3["BitShuffle"] FP3 --> FP4["TruncPrecision"] FP4 -.->|Reverse order on read| FP3 end subgraph ZstdPool["zstd_pool.rs"] Z1["Thread-local CCtx/DCtx"] --> Z2["Global pool (32 per level / 32 total)"] Z3["par_for_index
persistent workers"] --> Z4["oifs-chunk-w{N} threads
(num_cpus-1, clamp 1..15)"] Z2 --> Z3 end WritePath -.-> ZstdPool ReadPath -.-> ZstdPool ``` ## ZstdContextPool and persistent scoped worker pool `zstd_pool.rs` ([`src/zstd_pool.rs`]) eliminates per-call `CCtx`/`DCtx` allocation overhead through two layers: ### Thread-local context pools Each thread keeps one compressor per compression level and one decompressor in `thread_local!` storage. On thread exit (or explicit `release_pooled_contexts()`), contexts are returned to a global `Mutex`-protected pool for reuse by other threads: - **Compressors**: `HashMap>` capped at `MAX_GLOBAL_COMPRESSORS_PER_LEVEL = 32` per level. - **Decompressors**: `Vec` capped at `MAX_GLOBAL_DECOMPRESSORS = 32` total. The hot-path entry points `compress_frame(data, level)` and `decompress_frame_into(source, destination)` borrow from the thread-local pool first, falling back to the global pool, then to a fresh allocation. This avoids hundreds of kilobytes of internal table initialization per call. ### Persistent scoped worker pool (`par_for_index`) `par_for_index(total, f)` spawns `num_cpus - 1` worker threads (clamped to 1..15) named `oifs-chunk-w{N}` at first use. Workers park on a `Condvar`; each dispatch increments a generation counter, avoiding `pthread_create` churn and keeping thread-local Zstd contexts warm across calls. - The calling thread participates via dynamic work-stealing (`next.fetch_add`). - Falls back to sequential execution when `total <= 1` or another dispatch already holds the pool lock (`dispatch_lock.try_lock()`). - `workers_to_wake(total, num_workers)` computes the exact number of background workers to wake: `min(total - 1, num_workers)`, never waking redundant threads. - Kani proof ([`src/zstd_pool.rs#L399-L458`]) guarantees exact-count `notify_one()` wakeups can never deadlock regardless of how many workers are asleep. Used by: - Seekable chunked write pipeline (Stage 2 parallel compression/encryption) - Seekable chunked multi-chunk reads (`read_chunked_64k_internal`, `read_at_chunked_64k` fast path) - Sequential read-ahead prefetch in `read_at_chunked_64k` ## Compression modes and append behavior `write_data_with_filters` handles non-offset-0 writes with three distinct strategies for already-compressed files: ### Seekable 64K Chunked Compression (P4.2 fast path) When `INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K` is active or `CompressionMode::Seekable` is selected, writes enter the 3-stage out-of-lock pipeline (`write_chunked_64k_pipeline`, [`src/disk/chunked.rs#L1702-L1860`]). Only affected 64KB chunks are re-encoded and swapped via COW extents, eliminating full-file rewrites. ### Zstd Multi-Frame Append (stream fast path) When appending strictly at EOF (`file_offset == inode.size`) to an *unencrypted* stream-compressed file with *no* active filters, the new chunk is compressed as an independent Zstd frame via `zstd_pool::compress_frame` and appended at `compressed_size`. Because `zstd::stream::decode_all` transparently decodes concatenated frames, no existing block is decompressed or rewritten. ### Read-Modify-Recompress (stream fallback) For encrypted stream files, random-offset stream writes, or files with active filters, the full payload is decompressed, the change is spliced in, old blocks are freed, and the file is rewritten contiguously from offset 0 with an effective filter config that recovers the inode's stored filter flags. Raw (uncompressed) files use a plain in-place `write_buffer_at_offset` write that does not participate in the frame pipeline. ## Seekable 64KB Chunked Compression (P4.2) To avoid $O(N)$ full-payload decompression on random reads and partial writes, OIFS implements **Seekable 64KB Chunked Compression**: - **Fixed 64KB Logical Chunks**: Files are partitioned into uniform 64KB chunks (`CHUNK_SIZE_64K = 65536`). - **64-bit ChunkEntry**: Stored directly in the inode block table, each 8-byte entry packs `start_block: u32`, `block_count: u8`, `flags: u8` (`FLAG_RAW` or `FLAG_COMPRESSED`), and `compressed_len: u16` ([`src/inode.rs#L89-L119`]). - **Copy-on-Write (COW) Extent Swap**: Updating data at any offset (`write_chunked_64k_internal`, [`src/disk/chunked.rs#L1702-L1860`]) allocates new physical contiguous blocks, writes compressed or raw bytes, atomically updates the chunk pointer (`set_logical_chunk_entry`), and then frees the old blocks. - **Anti-Inflation Fallback**: If a compressed chunk does not strictly save space (or exceeds 64KB), it is stored as uncompressed `FLAG_RAW` blocks, eliminating negative compression overhead. - **$O(1)$ Random Reads**: `read_at_chunked_64k` ([`src/disk/chunked.rs#L591-L780`]) decodes only the single targeted 64KB chunk directly into the caller's buffer without decompressing the entire file, completely bypassing stateful file offset tracking. - **Sequential Read-Ahead**: For sequential sub-chunk reads, the read path detects the pattern (current chunk miss + previous chunk hit in cache) and prefetches up to 4 subsequent chunks in parallel via `par_for_index`, inserting them into `ChunkReadCache` under a single write lock acquisition. ### Mermaid diagram: Seekable Chunked Layout ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Inode["Inode Block Table"] D0["blocks[0]"] D1["blocks[1]"] D2["blocks[2]"] D9["blocks[9]"] SIB["blocks[10] (Single Indirect)"] DIB["blocks[11] (Double Indirect)"] TIB["triple_indirect"] end subgraph ChunkEntries["ChunkEntry Array (packed in leaf slots)"] CE0["ChunkEntry[0]: start_blk=100, count=16, flags=COMPRESSED, len=45056"] CE1["ChunkEntry[1]: start_blk=116, count=8, flags=RAW, len=32768"] CE2["ChunkEntry[2]: EMPTY (sparse hole)"] end subgraph DataBlocks["Physical Data Blocks (4 KiB each)"] B100["Block 100"] B101["Block 101"] B115["Block 115"] B116["Block 116"] B123["Block 123"] end D0 --> CE0 D1 --> CE1 D2 --> CE2 CE0 -->|"16 contiguous blocks"| B100 CE0 --> B115 CE1 -->|"8 contiguous blocks"| B116 CE1 --> B123 CE2 -.->|"no blocks allocated"| B100 ``` Each logical chunk index maps through the inode's pointer tree (direct → single indirect → double indirect → triple indirect) to a leaf slot holding a `ChunkEntry`. The entry's `start_block` and `block_count` describe a **contiguous run** of physical blocks storing that chunk's compressed or raw payload. ## Read acceleration caches ### DecodedBlobCache (non-seekable files) `DecodedBlobCache` ([`src/disk/caches.rs#L92-L163`]) is a bounded LRU cache for whole-file decoded payloads of **stream-compressed or whole-file encrypted** files. It eliminates the $O(\text{calls} \times \text{file\_size})$ full-file decode cliff when callers issue sequential or random sub-file `read_at` calls on non-seekable blobs. - **Capacity**: 4 entries (`MAX_ENTRIES = 4`) - **Per-entry limit**: 16 MiB (`MAX_ENTRY_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024`) - **Total cap**: 32 MiB (`MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 32 * 1024 * 1024`) - **Key**: `(inode_id, size, compressed_size, first_block, nonce)` — any metadata change invalidates the entry. - **Lookup**: Under shared read lock in `read_at_with_inode` ([`src/disk.rs#L3765-L3785`]). If present, slices directly from the `Arc>` into the caller's buffer. If absent and file ≤ 16 MiB, decodes the full payload, inserts into cache, then slices. - **Eviction**: LRU by insertion order; evicts from front when either entry count or total bytes would exceed limits. ### ChunkReadCache (seekable files) `ChunkReadCache` ([`src/disk/caches.rs#L1-L75`]) is an 8-slot LRU cache for **individual 64KB chunk** decompressions of seekable chunked files. - **Capacity**: 8 entries (`CAPACITY = 8`) - **Key**: `(inode_id, chunk_idx, raw_entry, valid_len)` — any chunk rewrite (new `raw_entry`) invalidates the cached version. - **Lookup**: `copy_slice_if_hit` copies the requested sub-range directly from the cached `Arc<[u8]>` into the caller's buffer under the shared read lock, avoiding `Arc` clone/drop atomic traffic on hits. - **Prefetch**: Sequential access detection triggers parallel prefetch of up to 4 subsequent chunks via `par_for_index`, inserting all into the cache under a single write lock. ### Cache invalidation `invalidate_payload_caches(inode_id)` ([`src/disk.rs#L644-L652`]) clears **both** caches for a given inode. It is invoked on: | Operation | Location | |-----------|----------| | **Write** (any `write_data_with_filters` path, including chunked) | [`src/disk.rs#L4856`], [`src/disk/chunked.rs#L1609`], [`src/disk/chunked.rs#L1957`] | | **Truncate** (`truncate`, `truncate_chunked_64k`) | [`src/disk.rs#L5841`], [`src/disk/chunked.rs#L1665`] | | **Delete** (journal replay of `SetInodeBitmap { allocated: false }`) | [`src/disk.rs#L2241`] | | **Migrate** (inode format v1→v2 rewrite) | [`src/disk/maintenance.rs#L119`] (`guard.clear_payload_caches()`) | | **Defragment** (safe mode live-reload, in-place defrag) | [`src/disk/maintenance.rs#L293`] (`guard.clear_payload_caches()`) | | **Reload** (after safe defrag atomic swap) | [`src/disk/maintenance.rs#L293`] (`guard.clear_payload_caches()`) | `clear_payload_caches()` wipes both caches entirely; `invalidate_inode(inode_id)` is the targeted version. ## Blosc2-style pre-compression filters `filters.rs` ships four composable filters (`FilterType`), each lossless except TruncPrecision: ### FilterType variants ```rust pub enum FilterType { /// First-order delta encoding Delta, /// Byte-wise shuffle (AoS → SoA transposition) ByteShuffle, /// Bit-wise shuffle (8×8 bit-matrix transposition per 64-bit word) BitShuffle, /// Floating point precision truncation (zeros least-significant mantissa bits) TruncPrecision { prec_bits: i8 }, } ``` - **Delta** ([`src/filters.rs#L249-L388`]) — first-order difference of typed elements (`delta_encode_inplace`), collapsing linear/temporal sequences into small integers. Optimized with SIMD: NEON (AArch64) and AVX2 (x86_64) carry-propagating prefix-sum for `typesize=1,2,4`. - **ByteShuffle** ([`src/filters.rs#L390-L478`]) — transposes Array-of-Structures to Structure-of-Arrays, clustering high-order bytes (`shuffle_encode`). Efficient for structured records (e.g., u32/f32 arrays where byte 0 of all elements are similar). - **BitShuffle** ([`src/filters.rs#L550-L630`]) — 8×8 bit-matrix transposition per 64-bit word using the symmetric Delta-Swap `transpose_8x8_u64` primitive ([`src/filters.rs#L522-L548`]). Effective for sparse/bitfield/boolean data. Involution property: `T(T(x)) == x`, so encode and decode share the exact same primitive. - **TruncPrecision** ([`src/filters.rs#L632-L695`]) — zeroes least-significant mantissa bits of f32/f64 (`trunc_precision_encode_inplace`); it is lossy, so its inverse is identity. ### FilterPipeline `FilterPipeline` ([`src/filters.rs#L19-L70`]) chains arbitrary filters in sequence: ```rust pub struct FilterPipeline { pub typesize: u8, pub filters: Vec, } ``` - `apply(data)` runs filters in declaration order (Delta → ByteShuffle → BitShuffle → TruncPrecision). - `unapply(data)` runs their inverses in reverse order. - `unapply_in_place(&mut data)` avoids an extra heap allocation when only in-place filters (Delta, TruncPrecision) are active. ### FilterConfig (compact inode representation) `FilterConfig` ([`src/filters.rs#L99-L186`]) is serialized into the Inode as four dedicated fields ([`src/inode.rs#L33-L65`]): ```rust pub filter_typesize: u8, // element size (1,2,4,8) — 0 = no filters pub filter_delta: bool, // Delta filter enabled pub filter_shuffle: bool, // ByteShuffle filter enabled pub filter_bitshuffle: bool // BitShuffle filter enabled ``` This avoids any per-inode heap allocation and makes the filter config trivially copyable with the inode. Factory helpers: - `FilterConfig::none()` — no filters - `FilterConfig::numeric(typesize)` — Delta + ByteShuffle (standard numeric pipeline) - `FilterConfig::delta_only(typesize)` — Delta only - `FilterConfig::shuffle_only(typesize)` — ByteShuffle only - `FilterConfig::bitshuffle_only(typesize)` — BitShuffle only - `FilterConfig::custom(typesize, delta, shuffle)` — arbitrary combination `FilterConfig::to_pipeline()` builds the corresponding `FilterPipeline` respecting the fixed order: Delta first, then ByteShuffle, then BitShuffle. ### Pipeline ordering `FilterPipeline::apply` runs filters in declaration order (Delta → ByteShuffle → BitShuffle → TruncPrecision), while `unapply` runs their inverses in reverse. The `FilterConfig::to_pipeline` builder respects the same order. ### Zero-copy application `apply_filters_cow` and `unapply_filters_cow` ([`src/filters.rs#L829-L855`]) return `Cow<[u8]>`: borrowed when inactive or typesize ∉ {1,2,4,8}, owned only when a pipeline actually runs. `unapply_filters_in_place` ([`src/filters.rs#L857-L865`]) reverses in-place for in-place filters, avoiding an extra allocation. ### Native C-Blosc2 integration When the `blosc2` feature is enabled, `blosc2_compress` / `blosc2_decompress` ([`src/filters.rs#L73-L95`]) build `CParams` with the compiled C-Blosc2 chunk codec, providing an alternative compression path that can apply Blosc2's internal filters and codecs. ## Entropy analysis and filter recommendation engine `calculate_entropy` ([`src/filters.rs#L668-L685`]) computes Shannon entropy in bits/byte (0.0–8.0). `recommend_filters` ([`src/filters.rs#L910-L1077`]) evaluates **14 candidate pipelines** against the input data: | Candidate | Description | |-----------|-------------| | Raw | No filter (baseline Zstd) | | Delta (typesize=1) | u8 delta | | Delta (typesize=2) | u16 delta | | Delta (typesize=4) | u32/f32 delta | | Delta (typesize=8) | u64/f64 delta | | ByteShuffle (typesize=2) | u16 shuffle | | ByteShuffle (typesize=4) | u32/f32 shuffle | | ByteShuffle (typesize=8) | u64/f64 shuffle | | BitShuffle (typesize=2) | u16 bitshuffle | | BitShuffle (typesize=4) | u32/f32 bitshuffle | | BitShuffle (typesize=8) | u64/f64 bitshuffle | | Delta+ByteShuffle (typesize=2) | "numeric" u16 | | Delta+ByteShuffle (typesize=4) | "numeric" u32/f32 | | Delta+ByteShuffle (typesize=8) | "numeric" u64/f64 | ### Evaluation strategy - For inputs ≤ 256 KB: evaluates on full data. - For inputs > 256 KB: samples three 64 KB windows (head, middle, tail, each 8-byte aligned) and scales projected compressed sizes by `original_size / sample_size`. - Each candidate: applies filter → zstd level 0 → measures compressed size, entropy, ratio, space savings. - Evaluation runs in parallel across CPU cores via `std::thread::scope` (not Rayon) to avoid external dependency. - The configuration with the smallest projected zstd size wins. ### CLI integration Backs the `filter-analyze` CLI command and `put --filter auto` ([`src/bin/oifs.rs#L583`], [`src/bin/oifs.rs#L863`]). Output includes a formatted table, rationale string, and Blosc2 filter equivalents for cross-reference. ### Formal verification (Kani) The whole filter family is covered by Kani bijectivity proofs ([`src/filters.rs#L1114+`]): - Round-trip proofs for Delta (u16, u32, u64), Shuffle (2, 4 byte), BitShuffle, composite pipelines. - Unaligned tail byte handling. - `transpose_8x8_u64` involution proof: `T(T(x)) == x` for all 2^64 inputs. - `delta_encode_inplace`/`delta_decode_inplace` with `typesize=0` panic-freedom. - TruncPrecision zero-bit identity. ## Extension seams Filters are layered on compression rather than fused into it: any new filter is a new `FilterType` variant plus matching (un)apply functions, and the pipeline applies and reverses them generically. `FilterConfig` is the single seam between the filter layer and the inode, so new filters require no changes to the write or read paths beyond adding the boolean/byte fields only if the compact config needs more independent settings.

nodes.title: Concurrency and session
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership

The session layer owns the process coordination contract while the IPC layer owns the transport. `OifsSession` ([src/session.rs#L60-L79](repo://src/session.rs#L60-L79)) decides whether a given process runs in **Direct (Master)** or **Remote (Proxy)** mode and forwards every operation to the right place. `src/ipc.rs` provides the `bind_or_connect` master election, the `IpcServer` request dispatcher, and the length-prefixed framing used on every hop. The actual mutation of the image happens inside a single Master's `DiskManager` (`Arc<RwLock<DiskManagerInner>>`), which provides shared parallel reader access and exclusive writer serialization with a dedicated `sync_mutex` for physical durability flushes.

## Session mode taxonomy

OIFS supports three **SessionMode** variants ([src/ipc.rs#L39-L52](repo://src/ipc.rs#L39-L52)):

| Mode | Transport | IPC Overhead | Use Case |
|------|-----------|--------------|----------|
| `Standalone` (default) | None — direct `mmap` | Zero sockets, zero background threads | Single-process, CLI, embedded, testing |
| `Local` | Unix Domain Socket in per-user private runtime directory (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/oifs` or `/tmp/oifs-<uid>/oifs`) | One background `IpcServer` thread on the Master; clients forward over UDS | Multi-process on one machine, containers, CI |
| `Network` | TCP + rendezvous `.image.master` file in image directory + **clock-free active Ping/Pong** probe | Master binds TCP; clients connect over TCP | NFS/Lustre, multi-node clusters, remote mounts |

**Standalone** is not a third variant of `OifsSession` — it is simply `SessionMode::Standalone` which produces a `Direct` session **without** starting an `IpcServer`. The `OifsSession` enum itself has only two variants ([src/session.rs#L60-L79](repo://src/session.rs#L60-L79)):

```rust
pub enum OifsSession {
    Direct { dm: Arc<DiskManager>, server: Option<Arc<IpcServer>>, ... },
    Remote { client: Arc<IpcClient>, dm_fallback: Arc<Mutex<Option<Arc<DiskManager>>>>, ... },
}
```

- **Direct**: owns the `DiskManager` (and optionally a background `IpcServer`). Used by Master in Local/Network modes, and by **all** processes in Standalone mode.
- **Remote**: holds an `IpcClient` connection pool to the Master, plus a `dm_fallback` slot used during transparent failover.

### Entry points

Each mode exposes a family of constructors on `OifsSession`:

| Mode | Open existing | Open with password | Create encrypted | Open journaled |
|------|---------------|-------------------|------------------|----------------|
| Standalone | `open` / `get_or_open` | `open_with_password` / `get_or_open_with_password` | `create_encrypted` / `get_or_create_encrypted` | `open_journaled` / `get_or_open_journaled` |
| Local | `open_local` / `get_or_open_local` | `open_local_with_password` / `get_or_open_local_with_password` | `create_encrypted_local` / `get_or_create_encrypted_local` | `open_journaled_local` / `get_or_open_journaled_local` |
| Network | `open_network` / `get_or_open_network` | `open_network_with_password` / `get_or_open_network_with_password` | `create_encrypted_network` / `get_or_create_encrypted_network` | `open_journaled_network` / `get_or_open_journaled_network` |

All `get_or_open_*` variants are thread-safe and deduplicate via the process-wide session registry (see below).

## Master election: `bind_or_connect`

Master election is transport-specific and implemented in `bind_or_connect` ([src/ipc.rs#L887-L1010](repo://src/ipc.rs#L887-L1010)). The function either binds as Master (returning `MasterOrClient::Master`) or connects as Client (returning `MasterOrClient::Client`).

### Local mode (UDS)

1. **Deterministic socket path**: `get_socket_path` ([src/ipc.rs#L123-L144](repo://src/ipc.rs#L123-L144)) derives `<private_runtime_dir>/oifs_<name>_<hash>.sock` from the canonical image path. The parent directory is created mode `0700`; the socket itself is created mode `0600`. A companion `.tok` file holds the session secret, also `0600`.
2. Process first **tries to connect** to the existing socket (up to 10 attempts, 15 ms apart).
3. If connection fails, it **removes any stale socket/token** and attempts to `bind`.
4. If `bind` fails with `EADDRINUSE`, it retries connecting (up to 15 attempts), then removes the stale socket and retries `bind` once more.
5. On success as Master: generates a fresh 32-byte session secret (`auth_secret`), writes it atomically to the `.tok` file, and starts the `IpcServer`.

### Network mode (TCP + rendezvous file)

1. **Rendezvous file path**: `get_master_info_path` ([src/ipc.rs#L146-L158](repo://src/ipc.rs#L146-L158)) returns `<image_dir>/.<image_name>.master`.
2. If the file exists, reads `MasterInfo { addr, pid, auth_token }` and runs **clock-free active Ping/Pong probe** (`is_tcp_master_alive`, [src/ipc.rs#L159-L179](repo://src/ipc.rs#L159-L179)): connects to `addr`, sends `IpcRequest::Ping`, expects `Pong` within 500 ms. If probe succeeds, connects as Client.
3. If probe fails or file missing: attempts **atomic `create_new`** on the rendezvous file. Winner becomes Master:
   - Binds TCP listener on `bind_addr` (default `127.0.0.1:0` — loopback only; non-loopback requires explicit opt-in `is_loopback_bind`, [src/ipc.rs#L160-L180](repo://src/ipc.rs#L160-L180)).
   - Generates `auth_secret`, writes `MasterInfo` with hex-encoded token to rendezvous file (mode `0600`).
   - Starts `IpcServer` on the TCP listener.
4. Losers read the rendezvous file, connect to the published `addr`, and authenticate with the published `auth_token`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P1 as Process 1
    participant P2 as Process 2
    participant FS as Filesystem (rendezvous / socket)

    Note over P1,P2: Local Mode (UDS)
    P1->>FS: connect(socket) --> fails
    P1->>FS: bind(socket) --> succeeds
    P1->>FS: write .tok (auth_secret)
    P1->>P1: start IpcServer

    P2->>FS: connect(socket) --> succeeds
    P2->>FS: read .tok --> auth_secret
    P2->>P1: AuthChallenge/Response over UDS
    P1->>P2: AuthVerify (mutual proof)

    Note over P1,P2: Network Mode (TCP)
    P1->>FS: create_new(.master) --> succeeds
    P1->>FS: write MasterInfo{addr, pid, auth_token}
    P1->>P1: bind TCP, start IpcServer

    P2->>FS: read .master --> MasterInfo
    P2->>P1: TCP connect(addr)
    P2->>P1: Ping (active probe)
    P1->>P2: Pong
    P2->>P1: AuthChallenge/Response over TCP
    P1->>P2: AuthVerify
```

## Process-wide session registry

`SESSION_REGISTRY` ([src/session.rs#L77-L81](repo://src/session.rs#L77-L81)) is a process-wide `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, OifsSession>>>` keyed by the **canonicalized absolute path**. `canonicalize_path` ([src/session.rs#L84-L131](repo://src/session.rs#L84-L131)) resolves symlinks (up to 32 hops) so all links pointing at the same image deduplicate to the same registry key.

`get_or_open_with_mode` ([src/session.rs#L195-L215](repo://src/session.rs#L195-L215)):
1. Acquires `lock_unpoisoned` on the registry mutex.
2. If a session exists for the canonical key, returns a `Clone` (which clones the inner `Arc` fields — threads share one Master with natural reference counting).
3. Otherwise, constructs a new session via `open_with_mode_retry`, inserts it, and returns the clone.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Thread calls get_or_open_with_mode] --> B[canonicalize_path resolves symlinks]
    B --> C{Registry has key?}
    C -- Yes --> D[Return Arc-clone of existing OifsSession]
    C -- No --> E[open_with_mode_retry]
    E --> F{bind_or_connect}
    F -- Master --> G[Create DiskManager, start IpcServer, Direct session]
    F -- Client --> H[Connect, authenticate, Remote session]
    G --> I[Insert into registry]
    H --> I
    I --> J[Return session]
```

## IPC frame protocol

Every RPC is a **length-prefixed Bincode frame** ([src/ipc.rs#L306-L335](repo://src/ipc.rs#L306-L335)) with a **128 MiB hard cap** (`MAX_FRAME_BYTES`). Frames larger than this are rejected **before any allocation**.

- **Encoding**: `bincode::DefaultOptions` with fixint encoding, trailing bytes allowed, and a per-frame byte limit (`frame_codec`, [src/ipc.rs#L331-L339](repo://src/ipc.rs#L331-L339)).
- **Thread-local pooled buffers**: Separate read/write buffers (`FRAME_READ_BUF`, `FRAME_WRITE_BUF`) reused across frames; large buffers are shrunk after use (`shrink_frame_buf`, [src/ipc.rs#L354-L358](repo://src/ipc.rs#L354-L358)).
- **Streaming read**: Payload streamed in 64 KiB chunks into the pooled buffer (`FRAME_READ_CHUNK`), never allocating the announced size up front (`read_framed`, [src/ipc.rs#L370-L403](repo://src/ipc.rs#L370-L403)).
- **Single dispatcher**: `IpcServer::handle_request` ([src/ipc.rs#L699-L780](repo://src/ipc.rs#L699-L780)) maps each `IpcRequest` variant to a `DiskManager` call. Logic is **never duplicated** across Direct and Remote arms.

## IPC authentication: challenge-response with mutual proof

Authentication is mandatory for all data operations. Ping is allowed unauthenticated for the active probe.

### Credential types ([src/ipc.rs#L432-L440](repo://src/ipc.rs#L432-L440))

```rust
pub enum AuthCredential {
    Password(String),      // Filesystem password (encrypted images)
    Secret([u8; 32]),      // Session secret published by Master (plain images)
}
```

### Handshake flow

1. **Client → Master**: `AuthChallenge { client_nonce[32], has_password: bool }`
   - Client sends a fresh random nonce. **Password never travels in cleartext**.
2. **Master → Client**: `AuthChallenge { server_nonce[32], salt[16], encrypted: bool }`
   - Master replies with its nonce, the image's encryption salt, and whether the image is encrypted.
   - If encrypted and client sent `has_password=false`, Master immediately rejects with "Password required".
3. **Client computes MAC**: `client_mac = BLAKE2b-MAC(key, transcript(0, client_nonce, server_nonce, salt))`
   - Key = Argon2id(password, salt) for encrypted images; key = session secret for plain images.
4. **Client → Master**: `AuthResponse { client_mac[32] }`
5. **Master verifies client_mac**, then computes `server_mac = BLAKE2b-MAC(key, transcript(1, ...))` and returns `AuthVerify { server_mac }`.
6. **Client verifies server_mac** — proves Master holds the same key, detecting redirection to a fake Master.

**Domain separation**: transcript includes constant `AUTH_DOMAIN = b"oifs-ipc-auth-v1"`. Direction byte (0/1) prevents tag interchangeability. Constant-time comparison (`ct_eq`) for MACs.

### Where the key comes from

- **Encrypted image**: `DiskManager` derives Argon2id key from password + salt at open time. `auth_key()` returns the 32-byte IPC auth key. Master uses this for all peers.
- **Plain image**: Master generates random 32-byte `auth_secret` at startup, publishes it in `.tok` (Local) or `.master` (Network). Clients read it and use as `AuthCredential::Secret`.

### Security properties

- Password never on wire (even encrypted).
- Mutual authentication — client verifies Master.
- Session secret is owner-readable only (`0600`).
- Per-connection 10 s handshake timeout (`AUTH_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`) prevents Slowloris.
- Max 256 concurrent unauthenticated peers (`MAX_CONCURRENT_PEERS`) bounds resource exhaustion.

## IpcServer architecture

- **Listener thread** ([src/ipc.rs#L1070-L1140](repo://src/ipc.rs#L1070-L1140)): non-blocking listener fd, `libc::poll` with 50 ms timeout, accepts connections, spawns **one dedicated worker thread per peer**.
- **Worker thread** ([src/ipc.rs#L1142-L1300](repo://src/ipc.rs#L1142-L1300)): per-connection authentication state machine; after auth, loops reading framed requests, dispatches to `handle_request`, writes framed response. Emits `SessionEvent::PeerConnected`, `RequestHandled`, `PeerDisconnected` via bounded channel (`MAX_PENDING_SESSION_EVENTS = 1024`).
- **Drop**: graceful shutdown — waits up to 1.5 s for active peers, then removes socket/rendezvous file.

## IpcClient connection pool

- **Bounded pool**: up to `MAX_CLIENT_POOL_STREAMS = 8` concurrent authenticated streams ([src/ipc.rs#L1407-L1412](repo://src/ipc.rs#L1407-L1412)).
- **Checkout protocol**: `CheckedOutStream` RAII guard ensures a stream is either in the pool **or** checked out for one RPC. On panic or I/O error mid-exchange, `Drop` closes the desynchronized socket and decrements `total_streams` — never returns a potentially desynchronized socket to the pool.
- **Lazy secondary streams**: Single-threaded callers use one socket; concurrent callers open additional streams on demand, each re-authenticating using the cached `ClientAuthCache` (Argon2id key or session secret, zeroized on drop).

## Transparent failover (self-healing)

A Remote session survives Master loss (crash, power loss, network partition) without caller intervention. Implemented in `send_request` ([src/session.rs#L768-L848](repo://src/session.rs#L768-L848)):

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as Remote Session
    participant Master as Master Process
    participant FS as Filesystem

    Client->>Master: RPC over UDS/TCP
    Master--xClient: Connection error (broken pipe, reset, EOF)
    Note over Client: is_connection_error() matches
    loop Up to 5 attempts
        Client->>FS: Re-run bind_or_connect (master election)
        alt Becomes new Master
            Client->>Client: Create local DiskManager
            Client->>Client: Pin as dm_fallback (lock_unpoisoned)
            Client->>Client: Set has_fallback = true
            Client->>Client: Serve RPC locally via handle_request
        else Connects to new Master
            Client->>Client: Update IpcClient to new connection
            Client->>Master: Retry RPC on new connection
        end
    end
```

- **Lock-free fast path**: `has_fallback: AtomicBool` checked before acquiring `dm_fallback` mutex ([src/session.rs#L773-L779](repo://src/session.rs#L773-L779)).
- **Fallback promotion**: When a Remote process wins election, it pins a local `DiskManager` as `dm_fallback` and continues serving locally — the session **becomes Direct** transparently.
- **Password persistence**: Remote session stores the password in a `Zeroizing<String>` for automatic reconnection ([src/session.rs#L75-L76](repo://src/session.rs#L75-L76), [#L664](repo://src/session.rs#L664)).

## Reader parallelism and lock hierarchy

Within the Master process, concurrency is managed by a fine-grained hierarchy ([src/disk.rs](repo://src/disk.rs)):

1. **Shared Read Lock** (`inner.read()`): Multiple reader threads calling `read_at` or `read_data` acquire a shared `RwLock` read guard concurrently, executing zero-copy memory reads with no reader-reader contention.
2. **Dedicated Flush Mutex** (`sync_mutex: Arc<Mutex<()>>`): Physical disk flushes via `flush_range` / `msync` acquire `sync_mutex` **without holding the inner write lock** ([src/disk.rs#L1560](repo://src/disk.rs#L1560), [#L5397](repo://src/disk.rs#L5397), [#L5468](repo://src/disk.rs#L5468)), ensuring durable background writebacks never stall concurrent readers.
3. **Exclusive Write Lock** (`inner.write()`): Allocation, bitmap updates, and inode commits acquire an exclusive lock during the commit phase, ensuring full mutual exclusion.

The `DiskManager` struct holds:
```rust
inner: Arc<RwLock<DiskManagerInner>>,   // guards all on-disk metadata
sync_mutex: Arc<Mutex<()>>,              // serializes msync only
```

## ReadSession and FileReadHandle: lock-free read path

`DiskManager::begin_read()` returns a `ReadSession` ([src/disk.rs#L4577-L4584](repo://src/disk.rs#L4577-L4584)) that holds the shared `RwLock` read guard for its entire lifetime. Batching lookups, inode stats, directory listings, and positional reads through a `ReadSession` eliminates per-call `RwLock` atomic reader-count cache-line contention across concurrent reader threads.

```rust
pub struct ReadSession<'a> {
    guard: std::sync::RwLockReadGuard<'a, DiskManagerInner>,
}
```

**Methods on `ReadSession`** ([src/disk.rs#L8308-L8400](repo://src/disk.rs#L8308-L8400)):
- `root_inode()` — returns root inode ID
- `lookup(parent, name)` — directory lookup
- `read_inode(id)` — inode metadata
- `list_dir(id)` — directory entries
- `read_data(id)` — entire file contents
- `read_at(id, offset, buf)` — positional read
- `open_file(id)` — pins a validated regular file into a `FileReadHandle`

**`FileReadHandle`** ([src/disk.rs#L8399-L8590](repo://src/disk.rs#L8399-L8590)) eliminates both per-call `RwLock` acquisition and `BoundedInodeCache` lookups:
- Pre-validates inode type and encryption state at open time
- Fast single-block `mmap_slice` and `read_at` for raw (uncompressed, unencrypted, non-seekable) files under `IoBackend::Mmap`
- Falls back to full `read_at_with_guard` for compressed/encrypted/sparse files

**Note**: Because a `ReadSession` holds a shared read lock, concurrent writers wait until all active `ReadSession`s are dropped. Keep sessions scoped to bounded read batches.

## Poison-recovered locks: `lock_unpoisoned` / `read_unpoisoned` / `write_unpoisoned`

Some mutexes guard **reconstructible in-memory state** (registries, caches, coordination flags) where a panic mid-critical-section cannot leave the data inconsistent. For these, propagating poison would permanently brick the subsystem — one unrelated panic anywhere would make every later acquisition fail.

**Helpers in `src/lib.rs`** ([src/lib.rs#L42-L68](repo://src/lib.rs#L42-L68)):

```rust
pub(crate) fn lock_unpoisoned<T>(m: &Mutex<T>) -> MutexGuard<'_, T> {
    m.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}
pub(crate) fn read_unpoisoned<T>(r: &RwLock<T>) -> RwLockReadGuard<'_, T> {
    r.read().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}
pub(crate) fn write_unpoisoned<T>(r: &RwLock<T>) -> RwLockWriteGuard<'_, T> {
    r.write().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}
```

**Where used** (recover from poison):

- `SESSION_REGISTRY` mutex ([src/session.rs#L285](repo://src/session.rs#L285), [#L304](repo://src/session.rs#L304), [#L311](repo://src/session.rs#L311))
- `IpcClient` connection pool mutex ([src/ipc.rs#L1443](repo://src/ipc.rs#L1443), [#L1454](repo://src/ipc.rs#L1454), [#L1480](repo://src/ipc.rs#L1480), [#L1618](repo://src/ipc.rs#L1618), [#L1646](repo://src/ipc.rs#L1646), [#L1758](repo://src/ipc.rs#L1758))
- Auto-defrag config/stats/worker mutexes ([src/auto_defrag.rs#L187-L215](repo://src/auto_defrag.rs#L187-L215))
- Async flush pending ranges ([src/disk.rs#L555](repo://src/disk.rs#L555), [#L580](repo://src/disk.rs#L580), [#L1563](repo://src/disk.rs#L1563), [#L5428](repo://src/disk.rs#L5428), [#L5471](repo://src/disk.rs#L5471))
- Decoded blob cache ([src/disk.rs#L3756](repo://src/disk.rs#L3756), [#L3761](repo://src/disk.rs#L3761), [#L4840](repo://src/disk.rs#L4840), [#L4845](repo://src/disk.rs#L4845), [#L9088](repo://src/disk.rs#L9088), [#L9221](repo://src/disk.rs#L9221))
- FUSE handle map, parent map ([src/fuse.rs#L2242-L2272](repo://src/fuse.rs#L2242-L2272), [#L2665-L2670](repo://src/fuse.rs#L2665-L2670))
- Sharded directory cache: `read_shard`/`write_shard`/`for_each_mut` ([src/disk/caches.rs#L233](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L233), [#L241](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L241), [#L251](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L251), [#L257](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L257))

**Where NOT used** (poison propagates, as required for on-disk consistency):
- `DiskManagerInner` RwLock — guards bitmap, inode tables, block allocation. A panic here could leave on-disk structures inconsistent; the process must fail fast.
- Inode cache shards use `.unwrap()` directly ([src/disk/caches.rs#L398](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L398), [#L403](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L403), [#L408](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L408), [#L416](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L416), [#L422](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L422))

## 32-shard lock striping for caches

Both the inode cache and directory cache use **32 shards** with **Fibonacci hashing** (`0x517cc1b727220a95`) for uniform distribution, eliminating lock contention across concurrent accesses to different inodes/directories.

### BoundedInodeCache ([src/disk/caches.rs#L354-L423](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L354-L423))

- **32 shards** (`NUM_INODE_CACHE_SHARDS`), each with independent `RwLock<InodeCacheShard>`.
- **Second-Chance (Clock) eviction**: each entry has an atomic `referenced` bit. On cache hit under shared lock, bit is set (`Relaxed`). Eviction walks the queue, gives referenced entries a second chance (clears bit, re-queues), evicts unreferenced.
- **Fibonacci shard index**: `(inode_id * 0x517cc1b727220a95) & 31` — consecutive inode IDs never map to the same shard.
- **Capacity**: `INODE_CACHE_CAPACITY = 2048` total, ~64 per shard.
- **Single-entry eviction**: Reaching capacity evicts only one entry (old behavior wiped entire cache).

### ShardedDirCache ([src/disk/caches.rs#L201-L260](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L201-L260))

- **32 shards** (`NUM_DIR_CACHE_SHARDS`), each `RwLock<FxHashMap<u64, DirIndex>>`.
- **Same Fibonacci hashing**: `(dir_inode_id * 0x517cc1b727220a95) & 31`.
- **DirIndex** caches positive lookups; promotes to `complete` after `DIR_INDEX_BUILD_AFTER_SCANS = 8` cold scans or a negative lookup.
- On encrypted filesystems, maintains both `stored` (ciphertext names) and `plain` (plaintext names) maps to skip re-encryption.
- **Lock striping** ensures `create_file`/`delete_file` on one directory never stalls `lookup`/`resolve_path`/`list_dir` on another.

### ChunkReadCache ([src/disk/caches.rs#L1-L60](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L1-L60))

- Bounded sub-chunk decompression cache for seekable 64K files (capacity 8 entries).
- Keyed by `(inode_id, chunk_idx, raw_entry_block, valid_len)` to handle multiple logical chunks mapping to the same physical block.
- Eliminates repeated decompression/decryption for small positional reads (`read_at` with `< 64 KiB` buffers).

### DecodedBlobCache ([src/disk/caches.rs#L62-L160](repo://src/disk/caches.rs#L62-L160))

- Bounded decoded-payload cache for positional `read_at` on non-seekable compressed/encrypted files.
- Keyed by `(inode_id, size, compressed_size, first_block, nonce)` — detects mutation across reads.
- Capacity: 4 entries max, 16 MiB per entry, 32 MiB total.
- Eliminates the $O(\text{calls} \times \text{file\_size})$ full-file decode cliff when callers issue sequential or random sub-file `read_at` calls on stream-compressed or whole-file encrypted blobs.

### FxHasher ([src/lib.rs#L101-L164](repo://src/lib.rs#L101-L164))

```rust
const K: usize = 0x517cc1b727220a95usize;
```
Fast non-cryptographic hash for integer keys; processes 8/4/2/1 bytes at a time with rotate-xor-multiply. Used as default `BuildHasher` for all internal `FxHashMap`/`FxHashSet`.

## Out-of-lock pipeline: filter → compress → encrypt

Write operations split into three stages so CPU-bound work happens **without holding filesystem locks** ([src/disk.rs#L5671-L5850](repo://src/disk.rs#L5671-L5850)):

### Stage 1 — Shared Read Lock (inspection)
- Acquires `inner.read()`.
- Determines write case (FullOverwrite / CompressedAppend / Recompress / Raw).
- Reads existing decompressed content if needed for splice/recompress.
- **Drops read lock immediately** after collecting all metadata.

### Stage 2 — Zero Locks (CPU-bound processing)
- **Filter**: `apply_filters_cow` / `unapply_filters_in_place` (Delta, Shuffle, Bitshuffle).
- **Compress**: Zstd multi-frame via pooled `CCtx` (seekable 64K) or single frame (stream).
- **Encrypt**: XChaCha20-Poly1305 with per-file AAD (inode_id + scheme) — stack-staged, zero allocation.
- Produces a `WritePlan` with final bytes, new sizes, encryption nonce, physical offset.

### Stage 3 — Exclusive Write Lock (commit)
- Acquires `inner.write()`.
- Verifies inode unchanged since Stage 1 (re-plans if raced).
- Allocates/frees blocks, writes payload at `phys_off`.
- Updates inode metadata (size, compressed_size, nonce, filter flags).
- Flushes via `sync_mutex` (range-based or full) **after dropping write lock**.

This three-stage design means:
- Concurrent readers never block on compression/encryption CPU.
- Only the short metadata commit phase holds the exclusive lock.
- `sync_mutex` serializes `msync` without blocking readers.

## Zero-allocation path resolution: `resolve_path_iter` + `resolve_parent`

Path resolution avoids heap allocation by iterating over `&str` slices directly ([src/disk.rs#L6437-L6620](repo://src/disk.rs#L6437-L6620)):

```rust
fn resolve_path_iter<'a>(
    guard: &DiskManagerInner,
    parts: impl Iterator<Item = &'a str>,
) -> Result<u64, DiskManagerError> {
    let mut curr = guard.superblock.root_inode;
    for part in parts {
        // validation, '..' rejection
        curr = Self::dir_lookup(guard, curr, part)? ...
    }
    Ok(curr)
}

pub fn resolve_path(&self, path: &str) -> Result<u64, DiskManagerError> {
    let guard = self.inner.read().unwrap();
    Self::resolve_path_iter(
        &guard,
        path.split('/').filter(|s| !s.is_empty() && *s != "."),
    )
}

pub fn resolve_parent(&self, path: &str) -> Result<(u64, String), DiskManagerError> {
    // splits once via rsplit_once('/'), then delegates to resolve_path_iter
}
```

- **No allocation**: `split('/')` yields `&str` views into the original string.
- **Single read lock**: entire resolution holds one `inner.read()` guard.
- **~11.9M lookups/sec** on typical hardware (benchmark: `cargo bench resolve_path`).
- `resolve_parent` reuses the same iterator for the parent portion, returning the final component as an owned `String` only for the filename.

## POSIX OpenMode and race safety

`DiskManager::open_file` and `OifsSession::open_file` provide POSIX-standard file creation semantics ([src/session.rs#L870-L888](repo://src/session.rs#L870-L888)):

| OpenMode | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `OpenExisting` | Returns existing inode ID or `ENOENT` |
| `CreateNew` | Atomically creates file or returns `EEXIST` (`AlreadyExists`) |
| `CreateOrOpen` | Opens if present, creates if missing |

Under concurrent execution, `create_file` uses **double-checked locking** within directory blocks: even under aggressive multi-threaded races on non-existent files, exactly one thread succeeds while contenders receive `EEXIST`, preventing duplicate directory entries or orphan inodes.

## Block-level merge policy and Copy-on-Write (COW)

All mutations funnel through the **single Master's `DiskManagerInner` mutex** (exclusive write lock). The merge rules are:

- **Disjoint byte offsets in the same block** merge in place — each write modifies only its own byte range.
- **Overlapping offsets** are **Last-Writer-Wins** because the exclusive lock serializes writes into POSIX `pwrite` semantics with no torn writes.
- **Seekable 64K Chunked Compression** uses COW: updating data inside a chunk allocates fresh physical blocks, writes the payload, atomically swaps the inode `ChunkEntry` pointer, and frees the previous blocks. Readers never observe partially updated blocks.
- **Stream compressed files** use zstd multi-frame append at EOF, or transparent read-modify-recompress for random offsets.

This single-writer model (enforced by the Master-Proxy architecture) is the **sole source of write serialization** — there are no per-block locks or finer-grained coordination.

## FFI integration: `OIFSReadSession` and `OIFSFileHandle`

The C FFI exposes the lock-free read path via opaque handles ([src/ffi.rs#L1345-L1540](repo://src/ffi.rs#L1345-L1540)):

- `oifs_begin_read(handle)` → `OIFSReadSession`: acquires shared `ReadSession` + pins `DiskManager` via `Arc<FfiSharedSession>` (field drop order guarantees read lock lives as long as handles).
- `oifs_session_open_file(session, path)` / `oifs_session_open_inode(session, inode_id)` → `OIFSFileHandle`: pins `FileReadHandle` with its own `Arc<FfiSharedSession>` so destroying the parent `OIFSReadSession` first does not invalidate the file handle (zero UAF).
- `oifs_file_read_at(file, offset, buf, len)`: zero-copy for raw mmap files, zero `RwLock` acquisition, zero inode lookup.
- `oifs_file_size`, `oifs_file_inode_id`, `oifs_file_close`, `oifs_end_read` complete the lifecycle.

nodes.title: Online Defragmentation and Auto-Defrag
nodes.description: How OIFS analyzes filesystem fragmentation using 64-bit bitmap scanning and performs both safe (out-of-place rebuild with atomic rename) and WAL-atomic in-place defragmentation, including ChunkEntry relocation for seekable files, shift_table_collapse for chunk table compaction, and a background auto-defrag coordinator.
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership

Defragmentation and space reorganization logic reside entirely within [`DiskManager`](repo://src/disk.rs). It evaluates disk layout health through [`analyze_fragmentation`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L137-L166), which measures free-block scattering across physical data space. Defragmentation execution is exposed via [`DiskManager::defragment`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L460-L480), supporting two operational modes:

- `DefragMode::Safe` (default): An out-of-place reorganization in a temporary image followed by transactional verification and a 3-step atomic rename with rollback.
- `DefragMode::InPlace`: Direct WAL-atomic modification of the existing image using round-based copy-on-write (COW) passes; directories and files are relocated into currently free blocks with metadata updates committed through the journal.

## Fragmentation analysis

Before and after defragmentation, [`DiskManager::analyze_fragmentation`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L137-L166) inspects the filesystem's `data_bitmap_block` using a read-only [`BitmapRef`](repo://src/bitmap.rs).

### 64-bit word scanning

Instead of checking bit by bit, the analyzer slices the bitmap into 8-byte chunks (`chunks_exact(8)`) and decodes them as little-endian 64-bit words via `u64::from_le_bytes` ([`analyze_fragmentation_internal`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L150-L255)):

- `word == 0`: All 64 data blocks are completely free. If not already tracking a free run, increments `free_runs` and extends `current_run_len` by 64.
- `word == u64::MAX`: All 64 blocks are fully allocated. Closes any open free run, recording `largest_free_run` and accumulating `total_gap_size`.
- Mixed word: Uses `word.count_ones()` to quickly tabulate allocated blocks, then iterates through each bit (`0..64`) with bitwise masks to track individual block boundaries and transitions.
- Trailing bits: Any leftover bits (`total_blocks % 64`) are checked at the end using `bitmap.get(i)` ([`analyze_fragmentation_internal`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L235-L250)).

### Metrics and fragmentation ratio

The resulting [`FragmentationStats`](repo://src/disk.rs#L157-L174) tracks:
- `total_blocks`, `used_blocks`, `free_blocks`
- `free_runs`: Number of separate contiguous sequences of free blocks
- `largest_free_run`: The size (in blocks) of the largest contiguous free chunk
- `avg_gap_size`: `total_gap_size / free_runs` (average size of free runs)
- `fragmentation_ratio`: Calculated as:

$$\text{fragmentation\_ratio} = \frac{\text{free\_runs} - 1}{\max(\text{free\_blocks} - 1, 1)}$$

If all free space forms a single contiguous run (`free_runs <= 1`), the ratio is `0.0` (optimal). If every free block is completely isolated (`free_runs == free_blocks`), the ratio approaches `1.0` (maximally fragmented).

## Safe defragmentation pipeline (out-of-place rebuild)

[`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L484-L640) reorganizes the filesystem out-of-place to protect against crashes, power failures, or corruption. The process executes across six distinct stages:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant DM as DiskManager
    participant Temp as Temp Image
    participant FS as Filesystem
    User->>DM: defragment(DefragMode::Safe)
    DM->>FS: fs::copy(source, .defrag.tmp)
    DM->>Temp: Open with preserved encryption key
    DM->>Temp: Scan inodes, preserve directory blocks
    DM->>Temp: Extract file data + compression/filter config
    DM->>Temp: Clear data bitmap (restore only dir blocks)
    DM->>Temp: Reallocate & rewrite files contiguously
    DM->>Temp: Flush
    DM->>FS: rename source -> .old
    DM->>FS: rename .defrag.tmp -> source
    DM->>Temp: Verify (open, fsck)
    alt Verification OK
        DM->>FS: unlink .old
        DM->>DM: reload_from_disk()
    else Verification Failed
        DM->>FS: rename .old -> source (rollback)
    end
```

### 1. Snapshot creation

The entire active image file is copied via `std::fs::copy(source_path, &temp_path)` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L498)). The destination defaults to `{source_path}.defrag.tmp` when no output path is provided. This guarantees that if the defragmentation process is killed mid-stream, the original image file remains untouched and uncorrupted.

### 2. Inode scan and metadata preservation

The temporary image is opened via `DiskManager::open_with_key(&temp_path, 0, enc_key)` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L501)), preserving the encryption key from the original image. Using [`BitmapRef::for_each_set_bit`](repo://src/bitmap.rs#L94-L108), all allocated inode indices are collected from `inode_bitmap_block` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L507-L512)):

- **Directories**: Directory blocks cannot simply be moved without updating parent pointer graphs, so directory block addresses are harvested via `collect_inode_blocks` and staged in `directory_blocks` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L514-L517)).
- **Regular Files**: For each file with `size > 0`, the file's exact compression status (`is_compressed = inode.compressed_size > 0`) and pre-compression filter configuration ([`FilterConfig`]: `typesize`, `delta`, `shuffle`, `bitshuffle`) are recorded ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L519-L526)). **Seekable 64K chunked files** are detected by `INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K` and their `CompressionMode::Seekable` config is preserved.
- **Inode Reset**: The inode on disk is zeroed out (`size = 0`, `compressed_size = 0`, `blocks = [0; 12]`, `triple_indirect = 0`) via `write_inode` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L528-L534)), freeing the blocks for contiguous reassignment.

### 3. Bitmap reset

The entire data bitmap of the temporary image is wiped using `bitmap_slice.fill(0)` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L537)). Then, only the preserved directory block IDs (`directory_blocks`) are re-marked as allocated ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L539-L545)). All other data blocks become completely free and unallocated.

### 4. Contiguous file rewrite

Files are streamed **one by one** from the original image into the temporary image using `read_data` / `write_data_with_filters` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L547-L559)). The first free block is always allocated for each file because the data bitmap is empty (except for directory blocks). This produces perfectly contiguous allocation for every file payload, all indirect blocks, and all seekable chunk runs.

### 5. Flush and atomic replacement

After all files are rewritten, `temp_dm.flush()` ensures all data is on disk ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L561)). The active `DiskManager` then executes a 3-step atomic rename:
1. `rename(source_path, source_path.old)` — original becomes backup
2. `rename(temp_path, source_path)` — new image becomes active
3. Open the new image and run `verify_integrity` (full fsck). If clean, `unlink(source_path.old)`. If verification fails, `rename(source_path.old, source_path)` rolls back.

### 6. Live handle reload

The original `DiskManager` calls `reload_from_disk(source_path)` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L628)) to swap its backing file, superblock, bitmaps, and caches to the new image without requiring the caller to reopen.
